verdict.rationale: Cua's own llms.txt calls it "Open source infrastructure for computer use agents" covering Spaces, Driver, Lume, the SDK and Bench, and a public GitHub repository exists at github.com/trycua/cua. The evidence never names the license, and it does not show which components (for example, hosted Spaces) are actually published as readable source. missing for 10: named OSI license (e.g. MIT/Apache), confirmation of which components' source is public, independent corroboration of the repo's open-source status.
